method: Direct view_image inspection of five contact sheets containing all 52 real UE continuous-playback screenshots, eight first-round gameplay sequence sheets containing 61 selected whole-viewports, and 11 original gameplay PNGs. No new UE launch by the reviewer, model change, or C++ change.

gameplay_sequence_review.viewport_crop: None; full original viewport proportionally resized.
gameplay_sequence_review.runtime_video_review_limit: The main task generated the current-run MP4. This reviewer inspected selected source screenshot sequences and does not claim to have played the MP4 or viewed all 504 source screenshots.

observations: Walk shows alternating leg poses; Run shows forward torso lean, bent-arm swing, a recovering raised short leg, and visibly different belly silhouettes while preserving a rounded body.
The visible eye and mouth region remains attached to the head in sampled side views. No obvious detached parts, exploding mesh, or large skin tear is visible.

Idle remains upright; Jump and Laugh original demonstration clips show small body/head changes from this gameplay side view. SingleNode playback holds the pawn at one location and does not demonstrate a physical gameplay jump.
The reviewed gameplay wall frames preserve the visible face/belly outlines without the prior cut-through appearance. Both facing directions remain readable, including shadowed portions.
The reviewed airborne frames show feet clearly separated from support surfaces; platform and early-landing frames show feet near the visible support plane and the whole character in frame.

No conspicuous discontinuity of the entire body silhouette is apparent in the sampled phases around natural animation wraps. Time continuity is separately confirmed by manifest values and is not a perceptual smoothness measurement.

First-round chronological gameplay samples show Idle to Run to Idle, reversal with the visible eye/head silhouette preserved, both wall contacts settling to standing without a face or belly cut-through, platform departure followed by airborne descent and standing, and successful platform/early-landing support poses.

The reset sequence includes a clearly visible PAUSED panel in frame_000140 and frame_000144, followed by its disappearance and a standing pawn at the reset ground position. The inspected panel and control text have no obvious clipping.
evidence_limits: Only the gameplay side camera is covered by the new playback. Fine mouth detail, front-view face binding, and every occluded region cannot be certified from it.

Actual playback screenshot intervals are about 0.194–0.400 game seconds. There are only 7–14 images per two-cycle clip; the 8 fps target was not achieved. Fine timing, acceleration, subtle softness, and high-frame-rate smoothness remain unmeasured.

This report views chronological real screenshots; it does not claim that an MP4 was played by the reviewer. No new independent-clip MP4 was generated in this audit; the main task separately generated the current-run gameplay MP4.
Physical keyboard input, window focus recovery, pause/resume interaction, and sustained hardware performance require the separate input/runtime evidence.
The reviewed gameplay PNGs predate this report by one local day. They are the latest successful recorded gameplay run available at audit time, not a newly executed 2026-10-13 movement test.

Gameplay sheets sample each case's existing screenshot sequence, rather than all rendered frames. Initial floating poses and changes of scenery at test-case boundaries can be test fixture teleports; this evidence does not establish natural camera transitions across test-case boundaries.

video_encoding.reason: Installed browser FFmpeg lacks concat demuxing and rejects -safe. Blender fallback exited 1 without output. Retained five successful sheets, complete manifest, and ffconcat timing files without pursuing encoder troubleshooting.

remaining_visual_work: No obvious image-level issue warrants another P0 model/render change. Higher-cadence perceptual polish is outside this limited acceptance; integrate with runtime/input acceptance before declaring full P0 completion.
